Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Persistence of AP-1-driven chromatin opening after stimulus washout
ideas.description: Pulse cells with a defined stimulus, then wash it out and track FOS/JUN occupancy (CUT&RUN or ChIP-seq) alongside ATAC-seq and H3K27ac at AP-1 enhancers over days. If AP-1 is a memory mechanism, enhancer accessibility and marks should outlast the decline in AP-1 binding, and the duration should scale with the length of the priming pulse. Chromatin scaffolding is the analogy here: the 'nucleoid-like' state is what carries the record.

ideas.title: Primed versus naive re-stimulation kinetics
ideas.description: Compare first and second exposures to the same stimulus after a rest period, measuring the timing, amplitude, and recruitment speed of AP-1 binding and target gene transcription (nascent RNA-seq, qPCR time courses). A memory mechanism predicts faster and stronger ('rearoused') responses on re-exposure, and this advantage should disappear when AP-1 binding sites are mutated.

ideas.title: Acute, time-resolved depletion of AP-1 during priming versus recall
ideas.description: Use a dTAG or auxin degron on endogenous JUN or FOS (or an optogenetic AP-1 switch) to remove AP-1 separately during the priming pulse, during the rest interval, and during the re-stimulation. Memory should be lost only when AP-1 is depleted during the interval or at recall, and not when depletion happens only during priming. This gives a causal test of necessity at each phase, rather than correlation.

ideas.title: Single-cell lineage tracking of AP-1 history across divisions
ideas.description: Combine a live AP-1 reporter (for example an FOS-destabilized GFP or an AP-1-responsive fluorescent sensor) with time-lapse imaging and lineage barcoding to ask whether a cell's prior AP-1 activity predicts its response to a later stimulus, and whether that predictive value is inherited by daughter cells. Quantifying this heritability (for example with variance decomposition) separates true memory from transient, stimulus-driven variation.

ideas.title: Mitotic bookmarking test of AP-1-marked enhancers
ideas.description: Sort or image cells in mitosis after priming and measure whether AP-1 and its associated enhancer marks remain on DNA through mitosis (live imaging of tagged JUN, mitotic ChIP-seq). Then check whether daughter cells re-activate target genes faster on the same stimulus. Retention through division is a strong criterion for a stable cellular memory, and loss of bookmarking with preserved memory would argue against AP-1 being the carrier.
